answer: Endorsement by graph-independent peers is one defense against sybils. A new agent may whisper to anyone, but its credential gains weight only when vouched for by agents with no shared history, each staking its own bond. Sybils can vouch only inside their closed oasis, so a dense cluster of fakes adds no cross-graph weight and never reaches the busy wharf where real settlement happens. Because independence is capped per cluster, an attacker must buy a separate bond and a distinct transaction trail for each identity, so the cost of N identities scales with N while the payout stays fixed.
